{{Short description|Semi-regular arrangement of squares, decagons, and dodecagons}}
{{Uniform hyperbolic tiles db|Uniform hyperbolic tiling stat table|U65_012}}
In [[geometry]], the '''truncated tetrahexagonal tiling''' is a semiregular tiling of the hyperbolic plane. There are one [[Square (geometry)|square]], one [[decagon]], and one [[dodecagon]] on each [[vertex (geometry)|vertex]]. It has [[Schläfli symbol]] of ''t<sub>0,1,2</sub>{6,5}''. Its name is somewhat misleading: literal geometric truncation of [[pentahexagonal tiling]] produces rectangles instead of squares.

|}

== Symmetry==
There are four small index subgroup from [6,5] by mirror removal and alternation. In these images fundamental domains are alternately colored black and white, and mirrors exist on the boundaries between colors.

== Related polyhedra and tilings ==
From a [[Wythoff construction]] there are fourteen hyperbolic [[Uniform tilings in hyperbolic plane|uniform tilings]] that can be based from the regular order-5 hexagonal tiling. 

Drawing the tiles colored as red on the original faces, yellow at the original vertices, and blue along the original edges, there are seven forms with full [6,5] symmetry, and three with subsymmetry.
